# Node SSRF report review — 15 October 2026

## Scope and conclusion

The ADP CI scan in run `38776186306` reported 26 critical-rated matches of
`tmp.gitlab.nodejs_scan.javascript-ssrf-rule-node_ssrf` (CWE-918). The rule assigns
CRITICAL severity to its matches; that rating alone does not establish an
exploitable server-side request. Review of the request construction, execution
context, call sites and redirect policy found the destinations below bounded by
existing controls. Deployment configuration is a trusted input; user/model task
content is not permitted to choose the configured service origins.

Sixteen results already carried Semgrep's `suppressions: [{"kind": "inSource"}]`.
Semgrep OSS 1.80.0 omits the optional SARIF status for a recognized `nosemgrep`.
The CI parser previously required `status: accepted`, so it counted those
suppressed results as active. Recognize the omitted-status convention only for
Semgrep / Semgrep OSS and only for `inSource`. Explicit rejected, under-review,
null or malformed statuses and ambiguous suppressions from other tools remain
active. Explicitly accepted suppressions retain their existing handling.

The other ten locations now have rule-specific inline review rationales.
Each annotation applies only to this SSRF rule at its reviewed call; the rule,
other rules and repository baselines remain enabled and unchanged.

## Additional match during validation

The repository-wide rescan of the isolated SSRF rule also matched
`modules/agent-factory/agent/src/complex-task-chat/gateway/chat-data-client.ts`.
Production constructors get the origin from protected `ADP_CHAT_DATA_URL`
bootstrap configuration. The constructor validates the origin; a private method
appends a fixed `/v1/chat/` prefix, and redirects are refused. Its existing URL
validation and capability-client regression tests cover this boundary. This
location receives the same narrowly scoped review annotation.

## Verification and limits

Parser regressions exercise Semgrep's real suppression representation, explicit
rejection/under-review/null states, external suppressions, other scanners and
unsuppressed findings. Source boundary tests cover GitLab/Vault destination
mismatch, permitted internal HTTP, GitHub origin/redirect behavior, provider
origin resolution, gateway artifact and knowledge clients, and the chat client.
Persona-operation tests additionally verify hostile endpoints are rejected
before credential acquisition or fetch, and caller fields stay in the body.
Reviewer tests exercise real loopback redirect targets and same-origin repository
renames. SDK tests exercise the test-owned loopback server.

The parser correction also recognizes two pre-existing HIGH inline suppressions:
`probe_historical_failures.py` intentionally executes definitions from digest-
pinned historical source, and `adp_cred/assume.py` intentionally execs the user's
explicit command with the assumed-role environment. Their source rationales were
reviewed; no new suppression was added to either. Other HIGH reports remain a
separate backlog. This review does not claim all repository security findings
are resolved.
